thread:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 — 480ms (baseline 220ms). p99 trending 1.2s. Alert triggered at 2026-11-03T09:01:34Z

maria: seeing the alert, looking at the dashboard now. any customer escalations?

ashwin: I got a few DMs from accounts in EU complaining about tokenization timeouts. Not full failures but slow tails. No obvious deploy recorded in the last hour.

josh: I can confirm increased TLS handshake times from our edge to backend in eu-west. Traces show extra cross-az hops for ~15% of requests.

maria: wiring up quick traces. hooking into x-request-id 3f6a... to follow a sample.

netbot: traceroute sample from edge-1 (eu-west-1a) -> backend pool shows unexpected hop to ccg02.gateway (different AZ) for subset of traffic.

ashwin: that smells like a broken BGP path or a regional anycast shift. Did infra run any route map changes?

elaine: No route-map changes on our side since last night. Cloud provider lists a partial routing event in eu-west around 08:55Z for a handful of POPs.

maria: ok, reproducing with a curl against eu-west endpoint with verbose TLS to capture handshake timing:

```
curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.eu-west.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

maria: sample output: `time_connect:0.042 time_appconnect:0.312 time_total:0.478` — appconnect is the expensive piece for the slow samples.

josh: ran `dig +short api.eu-west.redwood.example` on edge host. Some queries return 3.120.45.11 and others return 3.120.47.255; TTLs are low (30s). Mixed A records correlate with the slow traces.

ashwin: looks like we have two egress paths with different latency profiles; traffic is flapping between them because of low TTL and upstream load balancer health updates.

maria: for mitigation, we can: 1) increase DNS TTL to 120s for api.eu-west to reduce churn, 2) pin requests at the proxy level to the lower-latency backend for 60s, 3) add temporary traffic steering to preferred POP. Which is safe to do quickly?

elaine: DNS TTL increase needs a short change window but low risk. But provider-side routing instability might still flip both records. Pinning at proxy sounds fastest and reversible.

ashwin: agree. I'll push a proxy pinning rule to route 90% of traffic to eu-west-pop-a until things settle. Patch: set `upstream.prefer_pop = "eu-west-pop-a"` for route `/v1/*` with 60s sticky.

josh: deploying the proxy change now (canary 10%) then bump to 90% if stable. Deploy command: `deployctl update-config --service=edge-proxy --patch-file pin-pop.json --canary 10`

oncall-bot: Deploy started by josh at 2026-11-03T09:08:12Z — canary 10%

maria: monitoring p95 on canary slice. I'll post updates in 5m. Also enabling extra TLS debug logs for a short window.

(5m pass)

maria: canary looks good: p95 on canary 210ms, rest of traffic still at 480ms. Increasing canary to 90%.

josh: stepping to 90%... `deployctl promote --service=edge-proxy --to 90`

oncall-bot: Promotion completed at 2026-11-03T09:16:11Z

maria: after 90% shift, overall p95 dropped to 240ms, p99 to ~420ms. Good improvement.

ashwin: while that's stabilizing, I'll open a ticket with provider for the routing flaps and ask for their BGP dumps for the affected POPs between 08:50-09:10Z. Also requesting their internal health checks for the intermediate gateway ccg02.gateway.

elaine: let's also schedule a controlled DNS TTL bump to 120s once we have a clean window to avoid oscillation when we revert the proxy pin later. I'll prepare the change.

maria: for postmortem: collect the following — traces linking request ids to hop patterns, `/etc/hosts` dig samples, provider BGP dump, route maps during the timeframe, and our proxy logs with TLS timings. I'll put a checklist in the incident doc.

josh: reproduced TLS handshake slowdown locally using `openssl s_client -connect 3.120.47.255:443 -tlsextdebug -status` — server occasionally delays `ServerHello` by ~250ms when connected to the higher-latency gateway.

maria: notes: this looks like provider gateway queueing during route convergence. Immediate mitigation (done) is proxy pop-pin. Mid-term: small DNS TTL increase + fallback region steering logic for severe tail latency. Long-term: advocate with provider for routing stability or move some POPs to alternate provider in eu-west.

ashwin: also adding an automated detection rule: if p95 > 2x baseline and TLS handshake variance > 150ms across POPs, trigger auto-pin/steer to preferred POP and page network oncall. Will draft a PR for the routing-policy-runbook.

elaine: documented customer communication draft in #customer-success — we should mention transient routing issues and that we've applied routing pins to reduce latency.

maria: closing loop: no new customer complaints in the last 20m. leaving the proxy pin in place for 1h, then step down to 50% and evaluate. I'll update thread after removal.

(40m later)

maria: removing pin now — stepping canary down to 50% to test.

oncall-bot: Proxy canary update started at 2026-11-03T09:56:40Z

maria: after removal, p95 briefly rose to 320ms but settled to 250ms. Provider responded with BGP dump showing a flap tied to a transitory maintenance window at their POP; they've opened an internal RCA.

ashwin: closing action items: 1) PR for auto-steer rule (assigned ashwin), 2) DNS TTL bump runbook (elaine), 3) incident writeup (maria).

maria: thanks all. I'll create the incident doc and link to this thread.

josh: minute note — add a test to our synthetic probing that compares `time_appconnect` across POPs every 5m so we detect TLS handshake variance earlier.

elaine: noted. I'll sync with devex on adding that to the public status check page. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2026-11-03T10:12:45Z — monitoring continues.
